title: Ephemeral capacity-lease controller with latency-anchored geo pinning
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: We currently use long-lived geo-pinning and hard region affinity to keep tail latency low for customer sessions. Under cross-region incidents and bursty load this produces hard hotspots and elevated p50/p95 degradation in secondary regions. Goal: Implement an ephemeral capacity-lease mechanism combined with latency-anchored pins so that sessions get a short-duration affinity to a preferred region (to preserve latency), but the system can reclaim capacity quickly for global load shedding and failover while still meeting SLOs.

This ticket covers design + prototype + canary rollout of the controller and runtime hooks. Key ideas:
- Latency Anchors: compute a per-session latency anchor score (history-weighted p50/p95) and assign a pin TTL (30s-5m) instead of indefinite pinning.
- Ephemeral Capacity Leases: when a request allocates a slot on a region, it obtains a short lease token (default 60s) that the router tracks. Leases are renewable on activity; when capacity pressure occurs, leases are revoked in LRU-ish order for low-anchor sessions.
- Graceful Eviction Escrow: revoked leases enter a 5s escrow window where requests may be hedged to a fallback region or served by a degraded model variant to reduce latency spikes.
- Circuit Breaker Integration: region-level CBs will factor active lease utilization; when CB trips, we proactively revoke non-critical leases and shift traffic to compatible regions/variants.
- Capacity-awareness: router uses soft-thresholds (credits) to make admission decisions; leases act as transient reservations to reduce jitter from immediate admission denial.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Canary in one region shows reduced p95 increase during a simulated cross-region capacity drop compared to current global pin approach.
2) Telemetry emits lease-grant, lease-renew, lease-revoke, escrow-hedge events; dashboards show counts and latencies.
3) No SLO regressions for P0 customers during rollout (runtime-1.23).

Non-goals: This ticket does not change the model fallback selection heuristics or RBAC for Private deployments (those will be follow-ups).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Design sync: Team agreed TTL ranges and escrow window; Marcus to spike lease store prototype using Redis streams. Action: create API surface for router to request and renew leases.

2026-02-22 - Spike result: Redis-based lease store handles 50k QPS with ~600ns median extra latency. Prototype added at https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/5123. Note: need leader sharding for global scale.

2026-02-27 - Trade-off discussion: We debated placing leases in control plane vs in-path; chose in-path with batched lease commits to avoid control plane latency amplification. Recorded notes in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/EPHEMERAL-LEASES.
2026-03-03 - Implementation update: Router now emits lease-grant and lease-revoke events to metrics pipeline (edge.metric-events). Added feature flag ephemeral_lease.v1 for canary.

2026-03-07 - Load test: Synthetic workload (75k RPS, 30% long-tail) with region failover simulated. Result: p95 reduced by 18% vs baseline; however p50 increased by ~3ms due to lease meta checks. Investigating micro-optimizations.
2026-03-10 - Security note: KMS integration not required for lease tokens (they are short-lived UUIDs). Security reviewed ephemeral_lease.v1 flag and approved by security@redwood.com.
Planned next: Add automatic lease-prioritization heuristic using customer tier and recent error budget consumption; schedule canary for runtime-1.23 on 2026-03-20.
notes: Telemetry events: lease.grant, lease.renew, lease.revoke, lease.escrow_start, lease.escrow_hedge, circuit.breaker.trip, routing.handoff
Metrics to track: region_lease_count, region_lease_capacity_fraction, lease_revoke_rate, escrow_hedge_rate, request_p95_by_anchor, model_variant_fallback_rate
Dashboards: create 'Ephemeral Leases' panel under Console -> Routing -> Canary  (link TBD)
Simulations: run chaos testing for cross-region lattice where 30% of capacity is evicted and measure SLO breach probability < 5%
Runbook excerpt: On large-scale lease thrash increase > 2x baseline, toggle ephemeral_lease.v1 off and enable fallback hedging remote-only.
